drafted_from: tool:read-a-page-in-a-scriptable-browser's own row and its do-work script (tools/run-tools-in-my-signed-in-browser/do-work/read-a-page-in-a-scriptable-browser.mjs), whose tests run on a stand-in osascript; the Arc dictionary (tab URL, loading, execute, close) was read with sdef and the generated script compiled with osacompile; a live run on the person's Mac is not yet proved
start_here: Say to your AI: "Read the page at an address in my scriptable browser, signed in as I am, and give me its title, words and links", with {"url":"https://example.com/","computer":{"automate-an-app":{"app":"company.thebrowser.Browser"}}}. It runs tool:read-a-page-in-a-scriptable-browser and answers the page's title, text, links and images. It is the route for when no browser extension is connected to your computer.
no_lists_because: It names no list of yours: it takes its input, asks the browser app on your computer and answers, and keeps no row.
instructions: 1. Make sure the browser app (Arc, company.thebrowser.Browser) is open on your computer, and that the Mac app that runs tools is allowed to control it in System Settings, Privacy & Security, Automation.
2. Say to your AI: "Read the page at an address in my scriptable browser, signed in as I am, and give me its title, words and links", and give it the input.
3. The AI calls do_one_thing_in_my_account at @tools with method tools:run, tool tool:read-a-page-in-a-scriptable-browser and its input (the worked example shows one).
4. Read what comes back: the page in result, or needs_access "automation" with what to allow, or error "app_not_running" when the browser is not open (this run does not start it).
